title: Ambient principal affine neighbourhoods for finite sets in locally closed Proj subschemes
statement: Let $S=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}S_n$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring, let $O\subseteq\operatorname{Proj}S$ be open, and let $j:X\hookrightarrow O$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-proj] [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every finite subset $E\subseteq|X|$ there are an integer $d>0$ and a homogeneous element $f\in S_d$ such that $j(E)\subseteq D_+(f)\subseteq O$ and $j^{-1}D_+(f)$ is an affine open subscheme of $X$. In particular every finite subset of a scheme admitting a locally closed immersion into $\operatorname{Proj}S$ lies in an affine open. No finite generation of $S$, degree-one generation, base field, reducedness, or closed-point assumption on $E$ is imposed. The empty set is permitted, using the empty standard open $D_+(0)$.

source.place: Tag 01ZY, lemma-ample-finite-set-in-affine, proof of case (4), including the ambient standard-open choice; original field-quotient Step 10 uses this argument with S=e[x_0,...,x_n].

proof.text: If $E=\varnothing$, set $d=1$ and $f=0\in S_1$. Every prime contains $0$, so $D_+(0)=\varnothing\subseteq O$. Its inverse image is the empty open of $X$, which is affine by the standard-open and closed-immersion affine descriptions cited in Step 6. Hence assume $E\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 01ZY, lemma-ample-finite-set-in-affine, proof of case (4), with the standard opens chosen inside the given O.

proof.text: By clause (0) of the standard-open inclusion lemma, for each $x\in E$ choose $f_x\in S_{d_x}$ with $d_x>0$ and $j(x)\in D_+(f_x)\subseteq O$. Since $E$ is finite, this is a finite family and $j(E)\subseteq\bigcup_{x\in E}D_+(f_x)\subseteq O$.

source.place: Tag 01ZY, lemma-ample-finite-set-in-affine, proof of case (4), with the standard opens chosen inside the given O.

proof.text: Put $I=(f_x\mid x\in E)$. This is a graded ideal: in any expression $a=\sum_x a_xf_x$, its degree-$n$ component is $\sum_{x:d_x\le n}(a_x)_{n-d_x}f_x$, again in $I$. Every generator has positive degree, so $I\subseteq S_+$. By the description of Proj points, write $j(x)=\mathfrak p_x$ with $\mathfrak p_x$ a homogeneous prime. Since $f_x\in I$ and $j(x)\in D_+(f_x)$ means $f_x\notin\mathfrak p_x$, we have $I\not\subseteq\mathfrak p_x$ for every $x\in E$.

source.place: Tag 01ZY, lemma-ample-finite-set-in-affine, proof of case (4), with the standard opens chosen inside the given O.

proof.text: Apply graded prime avoidance to $I\subseteq S_+$ and the finite family $(\mathfrak p_x)_{x\in E}$. It gives $d>0$ and $f\in S_d\cap I$ outside every $\mathfrak p_x$. Thus $j(E)\subseteq D_+(f)$. All hypotheses were verified in Step 3; repetitions among the image primes cause no problem.

source.place: Tag 01ZY, lemma-ample-finite-set-in-affine, proof of case (4), with the standard opens chosen inside the given O.

proof.text: If a point $\mathfrak q$ lies outside $\bigcup_{x\in E}D_+(f_x)$, then it contains every $f_x$, hence contains their generated ideal $I$ and therefore $f$. Thus it lies outside $D_+(f)$. Taking contrapositives gives $D_+(f)\subseteq\bigcup_{x\in E}D_+(f_x)\subseteq O$. This ideal-membership argument is valid for arbitrary primes, without a closed-point assumption.

source.place: Tag 01ZY, lemma-ample-finite-set-in-affine, proof of case (4), with the standard opens chosen inside the given O.

proof.text: By the standard-open description, $D_+(f)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(S_{(f)})$ is affine. Since it is an open contained in $O$, it has the same open subscheme structure whether viewed in $O$ or in $\operatorname{Proj}S$. Apply the affine characterization of the given closed immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow O$ to this affine open: for an ideal $J\subseteq S_{(f)}$, $j^{-1}D_+(f)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(S_{(f)}/J)$. It is therefore affine, open in $X$, and contains $E$. This also proves affineness for the empty open in Step 1. Finally, a locally closed immersion factors as a closed immersion into an open $O$ by the definition of immersion, so the last assertion follows.
